ut_super_bowl_wall.blurb: A bolted wall tucked under a big roof at the lower end of Rock Canyon, east of Provo. Nearly all of the 13 climbs are sport routes, with a single easy trad line. The grades lean hard: about half sit around 5.12, a handful are 5.11, and only a few routes fall at 5.10 or below. The surface is a little loose in places but mostly cleaned up. Because the wall faces south it soaks up sun from late morning on and stays warm through much of the winter, so it suits cold sunny days better than summer afternoons. Expect it to be quiet. The walk from the lot is short and crosses a streambed that can run in spring.

ut_hidden_the.blurb: A limestone sport wall in Rock Canyon above Provo, reached by following the canyon trail past the water fountain and over two bridges; the face stands right in front of you after the second crossing. All 13 routes are bolted, mostly in the 5.10 range, with a few 5.11s and one or two easier lines near 5.8 and 5.9, plus one two-pitch route. The rock is good and the wall stays shaded for most of the day, which makes it a pleasant choice in summer heat. Routes are well protected, so it works for climbers stepping up into the 5.10s.

ut_memorial_day_buttress.blurb: A broad buttress high on the north side of Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Wasatch east of Salt Lake City. All 13 routes are trad, and several run to multiple pitches. The grades span 5.7 up through 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.10 and 5.11 range and only a few easier lines at 5.7 to 5.9. The rock holds up well even high on the face. It sits well above the road, and the hike to the base takes roughly 45 minutes, so this is a committing day for a party that wants quality, mostly mid-grade trad rather than a quick roadside session.

ut_trilogy_buttress.blurb: A multipitch buttress in the lower part of Rock Canyon near Provo, rising more than 600 feet. Most routes are bolted sport lines of three to four pitches, with a couple of trad routes and one top-rope option among the 13. Grades stay moderate, from 5.5 to 5.10, and most sit between 5.7 and 5.10. It offers some adventure away from the busy single-pitch walls. To reach it, head up the scree drainage east of Super Bowl Wall to where it forks; the main routes start on the left branch. The usual way down is to walk off to the west.

ut_blue_walls_the.blurb: A steep, slightly overhanging limestone wall in American Fork Canyon that faces north-northeast. All 13 routes are sport, and the grades are demanding: one 5.9 crack, four 5.11s, and eight at 5.12. The climbing is technical and sustained, a good fit for climbers working in the 5.11 and 5.12 range who want a mix of established lines and harder efforts. It lies on a hiking trail well up from the road, so plan for a real walk before you tie in. The canyon itself is known for pocketed limestone and plenty of trees.

ut_2_carrot_buttress.blurb: A prominent square buttress named for a carrot-shaped formation on its north side, in the Buckskin Gulch climbing area of southern Utah. Of the 13 routes, most are bolted sport climbs, with one top-rope line and one trad route. Grades are friendly, from 5.5 up to 5.10, with the largest group around 5.8 and 5.9. The limestone is vertical and technical, rewarding balance over strength, and chains at the top make it easy to set up a top rope. The trail to the base is about a quarter mile long. The cliff runs east to west, so sun and shade depend on the hour.
